A common behavior I witnessed on Reddit, and see less often on Voat (but still see), is when some user gets pissed off at another user and then proceeds to go through the user's comment history downvoting each comment from that user. The telltale signs are seeing the votes on each of the user's post history decrement by one shortly after the other user gets offended. Since voat doesn't have voting buttons while displaying the list of a user's comments this task becomes a little more difficult, but not untenable. I think it might be cool if voat made this behavior more difficult by limiting how many times one user can down vote another specific user in a given day (a rate limit, basically). Something like user A can only down vote user B x times per day, where x is the number of posts user B has made in the last 24 hours or since user A's last log on time, would largely prevent this behavior while retaining voting freedom. In pseudo code it would be something like:

function canUserBVote(userb,usera) {

userb.lastlogin = SELECT TOP 1 [login date] from [login table] order by [date] DESC;

usera.commentcount = COUNT [comments] from [TABLE] where commenter = 'user A'
 and [post date] >= GREATEST (userb.lastlogin, Now()-86400);

userb.downcount = COUNT [downvotes] from [TABLE] where commenter = 'user A' and
 user = userb and [vote date] >= GREATEST (userb.lastlogin, Now()-86400);

return userb.downcount <= usera.commentcount;

}

Then, before actually registering the downvote (or decrementing the vote counter - not sure how voat works internally), just consult this function.
Limit the number of times one user can down vote posts of another user.
